# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

For the November 4 fixed fit, the external concordance difference was small and its interval
included zero. The estimated
loadings correlated 1.000 with the unsupervised loadings at the unit survival weight. DeSurv
and elastic-net Cox trained on the same patients performed similarly. The joint coefficient
fit accounts for posterior loading uncertainty and uses a shrinkage prior. Calibration
slopes were closer to one in most series.

In the simulation cells with consistent recovery, the two-step fit already recovered the
prognostic program. The near-threshold simulations isolated a setting where supervision
could change discovery. Recovery and concordance improved when survival was strong, while
the differences were smaller at realistic survival strength.

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

Earlier analyses used external concordance to choose the gene screen, the input scaling and the rank carried into the November 4 fixed fit. Each series informed at least one development decision (@sec-external-uses), so no external cohort is untouched by development. The training-only rule of November 9 applies to choices made from that date. The inherited choices are being redone on training data (@sec-week-redo). The external results in this version describe a model whose setup was partly chosen on the same cohorts. The PACA-AU array and RNA-seq records both contribute to
the pooled estimate. The donor bootstrap and the donor-clustered HR intervals account for their shared donors
while retaining both series in the estimand. DeSurv used its published settings rather than a
new search on our training folds. `r nrow(ff) - cv_conv` of `r nrow(ff)` supervised training folds stopped at the sweep cap. In simulation the coefficients at $w_S = 1$ are
attenuated at the larger gene count. These studies use a common simulation generator.

## Continuing work {#sec-continuing}

Proposed supervision weights include a calibrated power on the Cox partial likelihood,
downweighting expression and normalizing the likelihood terms. Each would be assessed for
recovery, calibration, false activity and convergence before application to the real data.

The analyses of @sec-week take up three items listed in the November 6 version: a fitter for
several data types with shared activities and separate loading priors, the comparison with the
$\eta = L\beta$ parameterization, and rank selection on training data. They add comparisons
of the priors on the loadings and coefficients and a methylation-only fit. Once their results are reviewed, the
working model is fixed on training data and scored once on the external cohorts
(@sec-week-external). Every later choice follows the training-only rule of
@sec-external-uses.

# Appendix A. Model derivation {#sec-appendix-a .unnumbered}

The canonical single-modality procedure uses training expression $Y$ and survival times
and indicators. It returns posterior moments of $L$, $F$ and $\beta$, gene precisions
and the tracked variational objective.

1. Center and scale the input according to the training preprocessing recipe. Initialize the
   factorization using a truncated singular value decomposition of the resulting $Y$.
2. Compute the posterior mean and variance of $\eta$. Re-expand the Cox partial
   log-likelihood about the current mean predictor, using the diagonal curvature to
   obtain a working normal-means objective.
3. For each program, update $\beta_k$ using the first and second moments of $YF_k$.
   Update $L_k$ from the expression residual. Update the entries of $F_k$ using both
   likelihood contributions and refresh the projected scores within the loading update.
   Use empirical Bayes normal-means fits for the prior parameters.
4. Update the gene-specific noise precisions. Record the monitored objective including
   the weighted Cox term and the Kullback–Leibler terms. Rescale nonzero programs
   to unit training projection SD and check the relative change in the objective.
5. In each external series, apply the fixed projection loadings and coefficients to
   the available training genes. Harrell's concordance uses the direction learned
   from training survival.

The [full derivation](../../../derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivations/SSBMF-YFB-model-derivation-full.pdf)
gives the update formulas, the balance of expression and survival information and the
numerical checks. The companion `verify_derivation.R` evaluates individual updates against
the expected objective.

# Appendix B. Changes since the November 6 version {#sec-appendix-b .unnumbered}

- **External cohorts.** From November 9, 2026, the external cohorts only score fixed models.
  The rule and the DeSurv protocol it follows are stated in @sec-external-uses.
- **Model states.** @sec-model-states defines the model states behind the external results,
  and every external table and figure names its state in the caption.
- **Work of November 9–13.** @sec-week describes the week's analyses with placeholders for
  their results.
- **Summary, limitations and continuing work.** Revised to match the training-only rule and
  the week's analyses.
- **Wording.** The Kaplan–Meier captions and text call the November 4 risk score "fixed"
  rather than "frozen", to keep it distinct from the frozen $\alpha_F = 0$ benchmark.

No number from the November 6 version has changed.

## Changes between the October 16 and November 6 versions {.unnumbered}

- **Preprocessing.** Every RNA-seq cohort is logged once. The 2,218-gene set has
  `r big(genes$n_genes[genes$arm == "single"])` genes instead of
  `r big(genes$n_genes[genes$arm == "double"])`, `r big(genes$overlap_with_frozen[genes$arm == "single"])`
  of them shared.
- **Model.** The proposed model is the survival-weighted fit of @sec-model. The $\alpha_F = 0$
  configuration is a historical reference.
- **Objective.** The Gaussian log-normalizer in the activity KL is counted once per observation. The coefficient KL is exactly zero for a flat coefficient likelihood.
- **Orientation.** Two comparator scripts that chose each cohort's risk direction from its own
  outcomes now use the training direction. No reported concordance changed.
- **Sign correction.** The post-fit sign flip was removed from both fitters.
- **Simulation calibration.** Calibration slopes in simulation use exact event times.
- **Multimodal model.** Moved to proposed work.

# Appendix C. Earlier multimodal results {#sec-appendix-c .unnumbered}

The [October 16 writeup](../2026-10-16-writeup/writeup.qmd) records the previous
multimodal simulation and matched expression–methylation comparisons. The proposed
extension in this version uses the canonical single-modality objective as its starting point.
